body:
Call almost any government agency and you know what's coming: a robotic voice, a confusing menu, and a reminder that your call is important. You press 2, then 4, then 0 because none of the options quite fit. Then you wait.

If you can't stay on hold through your lunch break, you hang up and try again tomorrow. Some people never call back, and they go without the benefit, permit, or answer they needed.

According to the US Inspector General , in 2025, 25 million calls to the Social Security Administration’s number ended without service. People hung up, missed the callback, or couldn’t be reached. In January 2025, Social Security’s average hold times peaked at 1 hour 40 minutes. Service did improve by the end of the year, and the Inspector General credited a new phone platform and more automation for much of that.

Automation alone isn't the answer, though. At the IRS, the phone is still the main way taxpayers reach out, and in 2025 the agency began routing nearly 8 million calls to voice bots. According to the National Taxpayer Advocate's 2025 report to Congress , the bots answered only 29% of those calls. The other 71% were disconnected or abandoned, most likely because callers wanted to talk to a person. A scripted bot that can't understand people or finish the job just adds one more way for a call to fail.

This broken interaction is the front door to the government for millions of people. At ElevenLabs, we're working to fix that front door with voice agents that understand what callers need and can actually get it done.

## Where voice agents help today

Governments are already using voice agents for several kinds of calls.

## Answering and routing

The first job is replacing the outdated automated IVR phone menu. A voice agent can understand the question, answer it, or send the caller to the right department the first time. Think of a city's 311 line: an agent can handle routine questions and triage the rest, so staff can spend their time on calls that need human judgment. It can also answer in the caller's language and after hours, providing service to people who may need it the most.

In Ukraine, the Ministry of Economy's voice agent , built on ElevenAgents, answers the State Employment Service hotline 24/7 and hands calls to a person when needed. In its first 80 days it handled 2,698 calls, about a quarter of the line's volume, and cut the time to answer from 30–40 seconds to 18. When air raid alerts sent operators to shelters, the agent kept the line open.

## Status checks, scheduling, and service requests

Callers want to check where an application or refund stands, book or move an appointment, or update their information. These are among the most common reasons people call. The agent can’t handle them by talking alone: it has to verify who it's talking to and connect to the agency's systems. With that access, it can resolve the request instead of just passing it along.

In Poland, ElevenLabs powers the voice agent for Centralna e-Rejestracja , the central appointment system in the national e-Health platform. It calls patients who only have a landline to remind them of appointments and reschedule when they need to. With 40 million appointments a year and no-show rates of 10–20%, even a modest reduction in missed appointments can meaningfully improve access to care across Poland.

## Strengthening and protecting elections

In partnership with Brazil’s National Electoral Court (TSE) , we gave a voice to its Electoral Assistant, making election information more accessible to citizens. We also used our No Go Voices technology to protect the voices of several senior political figures, including presidential candidates, and Supreme Court justices, and blocked nearly 2,000 impersonation attempts.

## Guided applications

A voice agent can walk someone through a multi-step benefits or permit application, collect what's needed along the way, and hand it off to a caseworker when judgment is required. In Deloitte's 2026 Digital Citizen Survey of 1,000 Americans, 55% said they expect AI to improve public services, and 48% named step-by-step guidance when applying for government services as an important need.

In India, we recently signed a partnership with the state of Karnataka . We're working with the state's technology agency to explore voice AI pilots, starting with grievance redressal, public helplines, and entitlement schemes, in Kannada and other Indian languages among the 14 we support across the country.

## How voice agents improve accessibility

Language. According to the Government Accountability Office , 26 million people in the U.S. have limited ability to read, speak, write, or understand English. A menu with two or three language options leaves many of them out, and translation is expensive: the National Weather Service spent about $2.7 million between 2022 and 2025 to bring AI translation to five languages. ElevenLabs’ latest voice models support more than 90 languages, which puts language access within reach for more agencies.

Connectivity. Not everyone can just go online. The FCC's 2026 broadband report found about 10.5 million Americans still can't get high-speed home internet over a wired or fixed wireless connection, and more than 9 million of them live in rural areas. Pew Research finds that one in five rural adults relies on a smartphone with no home broadband. For them, a phone call is the front door, and in an emergency it may be the only one.

24/7 availability. Most government phone lines are staffed during business hours, and many people with jobs, kids, or shift work can't call then. A voice agent picks up at 2 am on a Sunday with the same patience it has at 10 am on a Tuesday.

## Why now: not every caller will be human

Government phone lines are already stretched. Soon, many of the calls won't come from people.
